Cargo hub maintenance in Memphis: SNT-TC-1A, NAS 410 or the airline's own manual?

Most Memphis candidates asking about aerospace NDT have one employer in mind: FedEx, which runs its largest hub at Memphis International Airport and maintains aircraft there. Aircraft maintenance works differently from aerospace manufacturing, and the scheme question has a different answer. Across the airfield the Tennessee Air National Guard's 164th Airlift Wing flies C-17s, and away from the airport the city's refinery, steel mill, power plants, rail yards and river terminals keep a large industrial NDT workforce busy. Here is how certification works in each.

On an airline's hangar floor, the maintenance manual decides

FAA does not certify NDT personnel. Advisory Circular 65-31B, issued in 2014, sets out the standards the agency will accept: NAS 410, ATA Specification 105 (the airline industry's own guideline), ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ISO 9712, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 and EN 4179. An air carrier picks one and writes it into the NDT section of its maintenance program and manual, and the inspections themselves follow the aircraft and engine makers' NDT manuals. So the useful question for a hangar job is not "NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A?" in the abstract. It is "which standard does this operator's manual name, and which revision?" Put that to the NDT Level 3 or the training department before you assume anything, and do not expect a certification from one carrier to transfer to another, because the employer issues it and it ends with the job.

Repair stations and component shops around the field

A Part 145 repair station follows the standard named in its own repair station manual and in its customers' contracts. That can pull one shop in two directions. Work done for an air carrier usually takes on the carrier's requirement; component overhaul done for an engine or equipment maker may arrive with NAS 410 or EN 4179 in the purchase order quality clause, flowed down the way it is for manufacturers. Eddy current and visual inspection on structure, and penetrant on parts, make up much of the daily method mix. The eddy current in aviation guide and aerospace penetrant testing page describe that work, and aviation NDT training covers the route in.

The Guard wing next door

Military maintainers on the C-17s work under their service's own technical directives, and any contractor supporting military aircraft works to the terms of its contract. Neither follows automatically from what a civilian hangar uses. If a defense contract reaches a Memphis shop through a prime, NAS 410 often comes with it, since NAS 410 replaced the old MIL-STD-410 in defense buying. Read the contract before you staff the job.

Off the airport, SNT-TC-1A carries most of the work

Valero's refinery on the south side, the Nucor steel mill, TVA and utility power plants, and the tanks and structures at the river terminals are inspected to API, ASME and AWS codes, and those codes call for personnel certified under an employer written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, or occasionally CP-189. That is where most Memphis NDT jobs sit, and the methods tilt toward ultrasonic and magnetic particle on steel rather than eddy current on aluminum. A technician who starts on the industrial side and later joins an aircraft employer, or the reverse, will be re-examined under the new employer's program.

Records that let you move between hangar and plant

  1. Course records with outlines, hours and the instructor's name for every method.
  2. An experience log signed by a Level 3 or supervisor, showing aircraft structure, engine parts, welds and plate separately.
  3. Every general, specific and practical examination result, with the procedure each practical followed.
  4. Near-vision and color records, kept current.
  5. Copies of each certification letter naming its standard and revision.

A new employer's Level 3, or a Responsible Level 3 under NAS 410, decides what that evidence earns you. Years under an SNT-TC-1A written practice, however clean the record, do not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement by themselves.

Where Atlantis fits in Memphis

For the industrial side of Memphis, and for anyone building toward an aircraft job, Atlantis offers training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. You work through the theory online at your own pace, with a line to our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT) whenever questions come up, use the aircraft hangar scene of the Practical NDT simulator between modules, and finish the hands-on work and the practical examination with your employer, under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Memphis. For repair stations and maintenance providers, our aviation NDT consulting covers written practices, procedures and Level I and II examinations, and for component shops facing customer audits we offer NAS 410 audit documentation support, preparing records your own Responsible Level 3 approves. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Memphis shops. If a component shop works to NAS 410, its RL3 decides whether outside coursework is credited, so check with that person before signing up. Read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A for the full comparison.
